title: Arithmetic genus of compactified generic isoresidual curves with two zeros and only simple poles on the Riemann sphere
author: Dawei Chen; Quentin Gendron; Miguel Prado; Guillaume Tahar
difficulty_reason: Adjunction and the published canonical-divisor formulas do not identify this generic residual fiber with the required complete intersection or eliminate its extraneous boundary components. The authors supply the full new arbitrary-linear-residue closure and level-by-level smoothing argument, then use the simple-pole boundary restriction to justify that identification. Their authored horizontal and vertical stratum enumeration and tautological recurrence evaluate the surviving intersections, giving the arithmetic-genus formula rather than leaving a new degeneration calculation to a reference.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem1.5: a1,a2 positive integers, a=a1+a2, p=a+2 labeled simple poles on CP1, signature(a1,a2,[-1]^p), and residue tuple outside the full resonance arrangement. The smooth multi-scale compactified fiber has 2g-2=a! times (a-(a+2)(a+1)/((a1+1)(a2+1))). Here g is arithmetic genus of the possibly disconnected compactified curve; the formula is not asserted separately for each connected component. Full new boundary residue analysis43–44 and horizontal/vertical intersection computation45–46 read. Necessary local new generalized residue smoothing and boundary smoothness18–23 read, as well as period and residue conventions3–12. Multi-scale compactification/local period coordinates from BCG and Benirschke, canonical divisor/tautological class formulas CMZ22 and the existing one-zero intersection CP25 are explicit named published foundations. No general higher-order pole genus, connected-component classification or wall-polynomial outcome counted; their remaining cores stay unreviewed. Entire74-page original retained, actual JEP13(2026) DOI10.5802/jep.339 and pinned dates.
